subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Endocrine Anomalies: Ambiguous Genitalia, GHD, and Cushing

steps.tx: Atypical development of external genital anatomy where chromosomal and phenotypic sex discord exists represents a medical and social emergency. The birth of an infant with **ambiguous genitalia in newborns** mandates rapid multidisciplinary evaluation by pediatric endocrinologists, geneticists, and pediatric urologists. A gender assignment must never be conjectured or declared until definitive chromosomal karyotype, pelvic imaging, and steroid biochemistry are completed.
steps.say: Ambiguous genitalia at birth is a medical emergency requiring urgent karyotype, ultrasound, and electrolytes. Gender assignment must be withheld until workup is complete.

vis.alt: Clinical examination schematic depicting diagnostic features of genital ambiguity including clitoromegaly, bifid scrotum, and hypospadias.
vis.caption: Clinical features of ambiguous genitalia showing bifid scrotum, micropenis, and perineal meatus. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Palpability of gonads within the labioscrotal folds or inguinal canals provides the most powerful clinical branchpoint in evaluation. The presence of **bilateral palpable gonads in ambiguity** virtually guarantees testicular tissue and male 46,XY disorder of sex development (DSD), such as androgen insensitivity syndrome. Conversely, absent palpable gonads strongly indicates a 46,XX infant with virilizing congenital adrenal hyperplasia, threatening fatal salt wasting.
steps.say: Palpating bilateral gonads indicates testicular tissue and 46,XY DSD. Non-palpable gonads strongly suggest 46,XX CAH, requiring immediate electrolyte monitoring.

rows: Testis on one side, streak/ovary on other
Mixed Gonadal Dysgenesis or Ovotesticular DSD

steps.tx: Deficient secretion of anterior pituitary growth hormone causes profound proportionate growth deceleration with preserved body proportions. In young children, **pediatric growth hormone deficiency** (GHD) presents with severe short stature with height velocity below four centimetres per year, delayed bone age, cherubic facial appearance with prominent frontal bossing, doll-like facies, and mid-facial hypoplasia, accompanied by truncal adiposity.
steps.say: Growth hormone deficiency causes proportionate short stature, cherubic doll-like facies, and delayed bone age. In neonates, it causes hypoglycemia and micropenis.

left.title: Neonatal Clinical Presentation
points: Severe refractory neonatal hypoglycaemia
Direct hyperbilirubinaemia (neonatal cholestasis)
Micropenis (stretched penile length <2.5 cm)
Midline defects: single central incisor, cleft lip

right.title: Childhood Clinical Presentation
points: Severe growth deceleration crossing percentiles
Height >3 standard deviations below mean for age
Markedly delayed bone age (>2 years behind)
Cherubic infant-like facial contours with high voice

steps.tx: Pulsatile physiological secretion precludes single random growth hormone measurements from establishing a diagnosis. Confirmation requires demonstrating **subnormal growth hormone stimulation testing**, where peak serum growth hormone remains below seven to ten nanograms per millilitre following two separate provocative stimulation pharmacological tests (such as clonidine, arginine, glucagon, or insulin-induced hypoglycemia), accompanied by depressed serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3.
steps.say: Random growth hormone levels are uninformative due to pulsatile secretion. Failure of growth hormone to rise above ten nanograms on two provocative tests confirms deficiency.

rows: Peak GH <7-10 ng/mL on two tests
Stable surrogate marker of GH action
Accelerates height velocity; continues until epiphyseal closure

steps.tx: Impaired antidiuretic hormone synthesis or action produces profound hypotonic polyuria and unquenchable thirst. In children with **pediatric diabetes insipidus**, deficiency of hypothalamic vasopressin (central DI) or renal collecting duct insensitivity (nephrogenic DI) causes massive excretion of dilute urine exceeding two litres per square metre per day. Children exhibit extreme polydipsia, preferring ice-cold water, nocturnal enuresis, and recurrent hypernatraemic dehydration.
steps.say: Diabetes insipidus causes massive dilute polyuria and extreme thirst for cold water. Central DI involves hypothalamic vasopressin deficiency, whereas nephrogenic DI is a renal defect.

left.title: Central Diabetes Insipidus (Neurogenic)
points: Hypothalamic-posterior pituitary vasopressin deficiency
Craniopharyngioma, histiocytosis, trauma, germinoma
Urine osmolality rises >50% after desmopressin
Excellent therapeutic response to oral/nasal DDAVP

right.title: Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus
points: Renal collecting duct resistance to vasopressin
X-linked AVPR2 gene mutation (85% of genetic cases)
Zero response to exogenous desmopressin administration
Managed with hydrochlorothiazide and indomethacin

steps.tx: Controlled fluid restriction followed by synthetic vasopressin challenge differentiates central from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. During a **water deprivation test in children**, fluid is restricted until serum osmolality exceeds three hundred milliosmoles per kilogram. Persistent excretion of dilute urine (osmolality below three hundred) confirms diabetes insipidus; subsequent subcutaneous desmopressin administration raises urine osmolality by over fifty percent in central DI.
steps.say: During a water deprivation test, urine remains inappropriately dilute. Desmopressin increases urine osmolality by over fifty percent in central DI, but produces no effect in nephrogenic DI.

steps.tx: Sustained supraphysiological glucocorticoid exposure produces a classic constellation of catabolic features and growth arrest. In children, **pediatric Cushing syndrome** is most frequently iatrogenic due to prolonged exogenous corticosteroid therapy for nephrotic syndrome or asthma. Endogenous causes include ACTH-secreting pituitary adenomas (Cushing disease), adrenocortical tumors (adenoma or carcinoma), and bilateral micronodular adrenocortical hyperplasia.
steps.say: Pediatric Cushing syndrome is most commonly iatrogenic from prescribed steroids. Growth deceleration combined with excessive weight gain is the most sensitive pediatric hallmark.

left.title: Characteristic Physical Phenotype
points: Truncal obesity with moon facies and buffalo hump
Deceleration of linear growth velocity with weight gain
Violaceous cutaneous striae (>1 cm wide) on abdomen
Hirsutism, acne, hypertension, and emotional lability

right.title: Screening Laboratory Workup
points: Elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol (UFC)
Loss of midnight salivary cortisol circadian trough
Failure to suppress cortisol on low-dose dexamethasone
Serum ACTH differentiates adrenal from pituitary etiology

steps.tx: Growth deceleration in the presence of excessive weight gain represents the most reliable clinical sign of endogenous hypercortisolemia in childhood. Unlike simple nutritional childhood obesity, where children are tall with accelerated growth and advanced bone age, **growth velocity in Cushing syndrome** exhibits severe progressive deceleration across height percentiles, combined with delayed bone age. Treatment of endogenous disease involves transsphenoidal pituitary adenomectomy or unilateral adrenalectomy.
steps.say: Simple childhood obesity features accelerated linear growth and advanced bone age. Cushing syndrome causes severe growth arrest and delayed bone age.

rows: Loss of diurnal rhythm; high midnight levels
